Consult Summary:
- Likely viral upper respiratory infection (common cold) with dry cough in a patient with diabetes and hypertension; symptomatic management advised; no antibiotics or prescription required at this time.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Cough and cold for about five days (start of weekend); symptoms include coughing, runny nose, muscle aches, headaches, chills.
- Associated symptoms: Dry, hacking cough; no sputum production; no shortness of breath; no wheeze; throat mild redness; no neck gland enlargement.
- Negative findings: Breathing reported as normal; no chest findings described.
- Past medical history and related medications: Type 2 diabetes on metformin; hypertension on lisinopril; able to monitor blood glucose at home; last blood pressure this morning within normal range; no documented drug allergies.
- Social history / preventive care: Not described.

Examination:
- Throat: mild redness at the back of the throat.
- Tonsils: not enlarged.
- Neck: no palpable cervical lymphadenopathy.
- Respiratory: patient reports breathing normally; no wheeze or abnormal chest sounds described.
- Vitals: not provided.

Impression:
- Viral upper respiratory infection (common cold) with dry cough; no signs of bacterial infection or chest involvement.

Plan:
- Symptomatic treatment: Night Nurse and Day Nurse products; compatible with current medications.
- No prescription or antibiotics at this time.
- Return precautions: seek medical attention if shortness of breath develops, wheeze occurs, or symptoms persist beyond three weeks; the clinician may re-evaluate including chest examination if needed.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: allergies; complete medications list with doses/routes/frequencies; vital signs; smoking status; immunizations; social history details; consideration of comorbidity management interactions with current meds.
- Internal conflicts: None detected.
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; some conversational filler and minor repetitions, but sufficient for note.
